jobs.title: Air Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
**Purpose**
  

The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer is responsible for preparing and submitting air quality permit applications for Teichert Materials stationary and portable equipment operations across California and western Nevada. The primary focus of this role is permitting: compiling emissions data for reporting, quantifying source emissions, preparing Authority to Construct (ATC) and Permit to Operate (PTO) applications, and managing them through district review to issuance.
  

  

This role serves as the company's technical resource for New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT) and toxics evaluations, CARB portable equipment (PERP) registration, and coordination with local air districts, the Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), and Northern Nevada Public Health. The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer supports facility\- and equipment\-level compliance, tracks permit conditions and renewal deadlines, and drives regulatory readiness and risk mitigation across the Teichert Family of Companies.
  

  

**Focus \& Scope**
  

*Essential duties and responsibilities, i.e. those which are basic, necessary, and an integral part of the job, are indicated below:*
  

  

**Air Quality Permitting and Regulatory Analysis**


* Prepare, submit, and manage complete and technically defensible air quality permit applications for new, modified, relocated, stationary, and portable equipment and sources, including Authority to Construct (ATC), Permit to Operate (PTO), and applicable portable equipment registrations.


* Quantify source\-specific emissions, including NOx, SOx, CO, VOC, PM/PM10/PM2\.5, and toxic air contaminants, using applicable regulatory methodologies, emission factors, and accepted calculation methods.


* Evaluate projects, facilities, and equipment to determine applicable permitting requirements, including exemptions, New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT), offsets, air toxics requirements, and other federal, state, and local regulatory requirements.


* Review draft permit conditions prior to ATC issuance, and negotiate practical, enforceable condition language with district permit engineers to minimize operational and compliance burden while meeting air quality standards.


* Manage permit applications through agency review and issuance, including responding to completeness determinations, deficiency notices, and technical inquiries; evaluating proposed permit conditions; and working with regulatory agencies to establish practical and enforceable permit requirements.


* Coordinate air quality permitting with California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review and other regulatory processes when applicable.


**Regulatory Compliance and Reporting**
* Maintain and administer air quality permits, registrations, compliance obligations, and regulatory deadlines for Company operations, including permit and registration renewals, monitoring, recordkeeping, emissions inventories, testing, and reporting requirements.


* Prepare and submit required air quality regulatory reports and inventories, including applicable criteria pollutant and toxic air contaminant reporting, CARB Criteria and Toxics Reporting (CTR), greenhouse gas reporting, and AB 2588 Air Toxics “Hot Spots” reporting.


* Administer applicable AB 2588 requirements, including toxic air contaminant emissions inventories, prioritization and risk screening, and coordination of required health risk assessments, public notifications, or risk\-reduction activities.


* Coordinate and oversee source (stack) testing for stationary equipment — scheduling required tests with certified testing firms, preparing and submitting source test protocols for district approval, coordinating district witnessing, and reviewing test reports for compliance with permit conditions and applicable emission limits.


* Monitor facility and equipment compliance with applicable permit conditions and regulatory requirements, including fuel usage, throughput, hours of operation, emission limits, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting obligations; identify compliance risks and coordinate appropriate corrective actions.


**Technical Evaluation and Field Support**
* Regularly access and evaluate active materials facilities, plants, equipment areas, and project sites to conduct source evaluations, obtain equipment and operational information, observe operating conditions, and support permitting and compliance activities (approximately 30% of work time, with the remaining time performing office\-based permitting, analysis, and reporting functions). Site conditions may include uneven terrain, stairs or elevated areas, heavy moving equipment, dust, noise, and outdoor weather conditions.


* Conduct or coordinate on\-site evaluations of Company facilities, equipment, and project sites to identify applicable air quality permitting and compliance requirements and obtain technical and operational information necessary to support regulatory determinations, applications, and reporting.


* Coordinate required source testing and other compliance evaluations, including test planning, regulatory agency coordination, review of technical results, and identification and resolution of potential compliance issues.


* Provide technical guidance to operations, equipment, environmental, and project teams regarding air quality permitting and compliance requirements so regulatory considerations can be addressed during project planning, equipment acquisition or relocation, installation, and ongoing operations.


**Agency and Organizational Representation**
* Serve as a Company technical representative and liaison with local Air Pollution Control Districts and Air Quality Management Districts, the California Air Resources Board (CARB), Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), Northern Nevada Public Health (NNPH), consultants, testing firms, vendors, and other external parties regarding air quality permitting and

jobs.title: Early Career Air Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
**Staff Air Quality Specialist – Portland or Lake Oswego**
==========================================================




**Maul FosterAlongi, Inc. (MFA)** is looking for a **Staff Air Quality Specialist** to support our air quality team in the Pacific Northwest. Whether you're based in Portland or Lake Oswego, you'll work alongside a collaborative group of scientists and engineers who are passionate about solving complex regulatory challenges and providing best\-in\-class service to industrial clients.


This early\-career role is ideal for someone with an understanding of air quality permitting and compliance who's ready to take the next step\-building technical depth, expanding client engagement, and taking on more ownership of tasks and small projects.




**As a Staff Air Quality Specialist, you will...**


dive into air quality projects primarily supporting industrial clients with permitting and compliance across the Pacific Northwest. Your days will be a mix of building emissions inventories in Excel, applying air dispersion modeling tools, interpreting environmental regulations, and helping shape project scopes, schedules, and budgets. You'll contribute to technical reports, join client and agency conversations, and play a hands\-on role in both the planning and execution of projects. As you build your technical skills, you'll also take more ownership of your work, managing tasks independently, reviewing deliverables for quality, and helping keep projects on track. Whether you're in the office or on\-site, you'll be part of a team that values curiosity, collaboration, and continuous learning.




**To thrive in this role, you must have...**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical or Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Meteorology, or related field with applicable coursework.
* Experience in air quality permitting or compliance
* Familiarity with emissions inventory development and air dispersion modeling tools
* Working knowledge of applicable air quality regulations at the federal, state, and local levels
* Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and ability to effectively use Excel for data analysis.
* Strong organizational and communication skills.
* An intellectual curiosity and drive to seek to understand.
* Ability to solve problems factoring in risks and benefits in decision\-making.
* Dedication to client deadlines and willingness to work overtime, as necessary.
* Ability to perform physical duties including, but not limited to, lifting, use of respiratory equipment and other protective gear, and traversing rough terrain.
* Experience with project scoping, scheduling, and budgeting a plus!

**Who we are...**


MFA is a multi\-disciplinary consulting company improving our communities through our work with our clients. We are employee\-owned and employee\-minded. Come join MFA for the benefits to your career, the benefits to your community and also our benefits package:

* 100% premium coverage for your medical/dental/vision and over 70% for your dependents
* Competitive paid time off plus nine paid holidays
* Comp time program for exempt employees
* Participation in the Employee Stock Ownership Plan
* 401k company match
* Support for your professional growth through coaching and external training support




**Our hiring process for this position**

* Initial Conversation with Recruiting/Onboarding Specialist
* Interview with Hiring Manager
* Interview with the Team




**Compensation Range**: $70,000 to $80,000\.




Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.




*Here at MFA, we celebrate diversity and actively encourage women, people of color, LGBTQ\+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, foreign\-born residents, and veterans to apply.*

*MFA is a proud equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to being an inclusive environment for all employees. Employment decisions are based on job requirements, business needs, and individual qualifications. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, marital status, military service, or any other status protected by laws and regulations.*

jobs.title: Graduate Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
SAGE Environmental Services (SAGE) is seeking a new team member to join our growing, busy practice. SAGE is a highly successful, women run business located in NSW, VIC and QLD. We are specialists in contaminated land and environmental consulting, and pride ourselves in delivering high\-quality, pragmatic solutions for our clients. Our core services include:

· Contaminated land environmental auditing and due diligence

· Human Health and Ecological Risk Assessment

· Environmental laboratory auditing and compliance

· Environmental site assessment and remediation

· Health Impact Assessments supporting Environmental Impact Statement (EIS)

· Independent verification, strategy, and contestability

· Expert witness advice

· Cross government collaboration

· Hydrogeology including groundwater modelling

SAGE is looking to hear from recent graduates and early career professionals (1\-2 years’ experience) to join our growing team in Melbourne, or Mooloolaba, with qualifications in environmental engineering / science. We are looking for someone to join our team who:

· Can work independently, including working from home if/as required.

· Is interested a dynamic work environment which includes field, laboratory, and office\-based work.

· Has excellent written and oral communication skills with strong research capabilities.

· Is highly organised, self\-motivated and outcomes oriented.

· Has relevant tertiary qualifications preferably in environmental engineering/ science.

· Is keen to learn and develop skills in all aspects of contaminated land consulting.

· Is available to work on a full\-time basis.

· Has a current Australian driver’s licence.

· Has previous work experience. Experience within environmental consulting or similar industries is highly desirable but not mandatory.

SAGE can offer the following benefits:

· Field, laboratory, and project\-based training will be offered.

· Mentoring and training with industry sector leaders.

· Industry networking with other graduates from the industry.

· Flexible working hours and remote working.

HOW TO APPLY:

Please send a recent resume and cover letter outlining how you meet the position criteria to careers@sageenvironmentalservices.com.au Applications will be assessed as they come in / Applications close October 8th.

Pay: $70,000\.00 – $90,000\.00 per year

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Richmond VIC 3121
